FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A42
The rear seat is the safest riding position for a child of any age. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A42
Never install a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger airbag. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A42
Follow both the vehicle manual and child-restraint instructions, secure the seat correctly and buckle the child into it. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A42
The manual advises rear-facing travel in the back seat for children younger than 2. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A42
An unrestrained occupant can be injured or killed by an airbag. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A42
An infant must not ride in the front seat of a vehicle fitted with a passenger-side airbag. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A42
Drivers and front passengers should sit as far from the wheel or dashboard as possible, especially if short, pregnant or elderly. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A42
A child safety seat is defined as one meeting Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A42
The defined federally approved child-restraint system elevates a child for correct use of a lap-and-shoulder belt and meets Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A42
In a vehicle federally required to have safety belts, the operator must secure a child weighing less than 55 pounds in a child safety seat. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A43
The operator must secure a child younger than 8 who weighs at least 55 but less than 80 pounds in a federally approved child-restraint system. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A43
A passenger younger than 18 must use a seat belt when older than 8 or taller than 4 feet 9 inches, unless a child seat or child-restraint system is still required. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A43
A passenger aged 18 or older must be properly belted in a vehicle federally required to have seat belts. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A43
The operator of a vehicle federally required to have seat belts must wear the operator’s own belt, subject to the stated exceptions. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A43
A United States Postal Service rural carrier is exempt from belt use while delivering mail. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A43
A taxi or limousine operator is not responsible for fastening the belt of a fare-paying passenger. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A43
A newspaper deliverer is exempt from belt use during actual delivery or duties requiring frequent vehicle entry and exit. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]
